title: Kenyan Coconut Prawns
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN080 (Coconut Prawns) and KEN079 (Prawn Curry) are both Swahili coastal prawn dishes. Prawn curry uses a tomato-based sauce; coconut prawns replaces the tomato base with coconut milk for a creamier, sweeter, more fragrant result. Both are quick and luxurious — the coconut version is the more celebratory of the two.

desc: Kenyan Coconut Prawns — fresh prawns cooked in a creamy, fragrant coconut milk sauce with garlic, ginger, tomatoes, and Swahili coastal spices. The most luxurious quick dish of the Kenyan coast — ready in 20 minutes and tasting like a celebration.
longDesc: Uduvi wa Nazi brings together two of the Kenyan coast's greatest ingredients — fresh Indian Ocean prawns and thick coconut milk — in a dish that is simultaneously elegant and effortless. The coconut milk creates a naturally sweet, creamy sauce that envelops the prawns without overwhelming their delicate flavour. Served with coconut rice, it is the coastal celebration meal at its most irresistible.
ingredients: 500g large prawns — peeled and deveined, tails on
½ tsp sugar — optional, to balance the coconut
steps: Season prawns with salt, turmeric, and paprika.
Cook onions in oil over medium heat until soft and golden — 6 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes. Cook for 5—6 minutes until softened.
Add curry powder and remaining spices. Stir 30 seconds.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir gently. Bring to a gentle simmer — do not boil hard.
Add prawns. Cook for 3—5 minutes until pink and just cooked through.
Add lemon juice, sugar if using, and coriander.
chefTips: Never boil the coconut milk hard — it splits. A gentle simmer is the key.
Do not overcook the prawns — 3—5 minutes maximum.
A pinch of sugar balances the coconut milk beautifully without making the dish sweet.
commonMistakes: Boiling the coconut milk vigorously — it separates into oil and water.

faqs.q: Can I use shrimp instead of prawns?
faqs.a: Yes — large shrimp work well. Reduce cooking time to 2—3 minutes as they are smaller and cook faster.

cookingScience: The fat in coconut milk coats the prawn proteins and helps them retain moisture during brief cooking. The emulsified structure of coconut milk also creates a naturally thick, creamy sauce without any thickening agents — provided it is not boiled hard, which breaks the emulsion.
sustainabilityTips: Source prawns from local Kenyan coastal fisheries when possible.
Choose coconut milk from sustainably grown coconut palms.
healthBenefits: Garlic and ginger add antioxidant benefits.
culturalNote: Coconut prawns represent the pinnacle of everyday Swahili coastal cooking — two abundant coastal ingredients (prawns from the Indian Ocean, coconuts from the palm-lined shore) combined in a dish that is both quick and celebratory. In Mombasa, this dish symbolises the generosity and warmth of coastal Kenyan hospitality.
regionalVariations: Spicy coconut prawns with extra chilli.
Dry coconut prawns — sauce reduced to a glaze.
